# Index of Major Examples

Find a case here when you remember the situation more readily than the concept. **Evidence role** identifies the kind of example or study.

## Recurring case map

When a case returns, look for the new question it helps answer.

| Recurring case | Introduced | What later chapters add |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Hiring and selection** | Chapter 1 asks what made one candidate preferable; Chapter 2 widens the alternatives and makes the trade-offs visible. | Which evidence was noticed? How do comparisons and group discussion change the judgment? Chapter 41 brings these questions into a reviewable hiring process. |
| **Supplier capacity and project risk** | Chapter 18 asks what a reassuring supplier record leaves unobserved. | Chapters 35–38 uncover why a supplier refuses an offer, build a workable package, and specify what happens when forecasts or deliveries fail. |
| **Defensive workplace conversation** | Chapters 33–34 examine an ambiguous accountability message, a missed deadline, and the repair that follows. | Chapter 39 changes the conditions surrounding a defensive response; Chapter 41 protects dissent and learning within the organization. |
| **Employment or service agreement** | Chapter 2 treats accepting an offer as one option among several possible actions. | Chapters 35–38 ask what each side can do without agreement, which differences permit a better package, and how the agreement will work. |
| **Retirement or subscription path** | Chapters 19–20 examine delay and the way money is mentally labelled. | Chapter 40 follows the actual enrollment or cancellation path and examines defaults, effort, transparency, and exit. |

: Five recurring cases and the new analytical layer added when each returns. {#tbl-recurring-case-map}
